response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, o.recordvault AS recordvault, AVG(f.feerate) - AVG(f.rebrate) AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope, o.recordvault), per_scope AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM per_order WHERE net_rate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, order_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_of_scope_avgs FROM per_scope

assumptions.assumption: An order's net rate is AVG(feerate) minus AVG(rebrate) over its fee records, with NULLs ignored inside each average. If either average is NULL, the order's net rate is missing and the order is dropped.
The order count per scope counts only orders that have a non-missing net rate, i.e. the orders actually averaged.
orders.recordvault and users.userstamp are unique, so the joins do not duplicate orders.
The comparison baseline is the unweighted mean of the per-scope average net rates, taken across the scopes that appear in the output.
